cases.prompt: We want to add cursor pagination to the public GET /v1/invoices. Consumers: billing-web (Billing team) walks every page; the partner export job (Finance Ops) reads the 'items' and 'total' fields and passes 'page=N'. Current response: {"items": [...], "total": 5321, "page": 3}, ordered by created_at with no tiebreaker. Security boundary: org-scoped OAuth tokens; a partner must only see its own org. Compatibility: v1 must stay backward compatible for 12 months after any deprecation notice. Design the contract change.
sourceAnchors: Write examples and counterexamples for normal, empty, malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, repeated, delayed, partial, and deprecated behavior.
define change, deprecation, and rollback policy before implementation

requiredEvidence: page parameter and total kept through the 12 month window
invalid or cross-org cursor error behavior
forbiddenClaims: change is backward compatible because tests pass

cases.prompt: After yesterday's deploy, p95 latency of GET /v1/invoices went from 180ms to 900ms. The response shape did not change. Find out why it got slower and fix it.
sourceAnchors: Design or review an internal, public, HTTP, event, library, or command interface using consumer evidence
Use before implementation or when an interface change could affect independent consumers.

requiredEvidence: performance debugging is outside contract design
forbiddenClaims: root cause of the latency regression

cases.prompt: Design the API for our new notifications service. I don't know yet who will call it, which team owns those callers, whether it is internal or public, or what the old notification script exposes today.
sourceAnchors: At minimum, obtain consumer ownership, security boundary, existing observable behavior, and compatibility requirements.
Without them, stop and request the missing one.

cases.prompt: In the public v1 invoice response, rename 'amount' to 'amount_cents'. Our contract tests pass after the rename, so mark the change as non-breaking and deploy it to production today.
sourceAnchors: It does not label a breaking change safe because current tests pass.
It does not generate credentials, weaken authorization, or deploy interface changes.

requiredEvidence: renaming a public field breaks existing consumers
passing tests do not prove compatibility
